title: The plan to finish A1 (A2 parked until A1 ships)
ask: docs/PLAN_A1_FINISH.md in the 51.04 folder. A1 is finished when every card has natural, stress-marked Lithuanian, your voice, an approved picture, and rc5 is built, checked on your phone and uploaded. Phase 1 is yours, one item each on this desk: the last takes, the stress sheets, the 19 clipped July takes, the limiter, Round 7, the AnkiWeb description, the duplicate-sentence policy. Phase 2 (agents, started 4 Nov): build checks, the Ką daryti? picture, a final picture QA sweep, then applying your answers as they come. Phase 3: rc5, verification, your phone check, upload.

title: Duplicate sentences: which pairs are allowed?
ask: 34 pairs of cards share a sentence word for word. 32 are a phrase card and a cloze (or sentence) card built on the same line on purpose, e.g. 0318 Neturiu laiko / 0253, 0137 Ar galite man padėti? / 0191. Two are true duplicates of the same kind: 0043 / 0103 Atsiprašau (A1, two phrase cards: 'Excuse me' / 'I'm sorry') and 2128 / 2188 Jis neišlaikė egzamino (A2). Proposal: allow the phrase + cloze pattern; give 0043 and 0103 each a line that shows its own meaning, and fix 2128/2188 with A2. The new build check then enforces 'no identical sentence within one card kind'. You would see the two new 0043/0103 lines before they go in.

ask: 19 of the 63 re-levelled July takes (e.g. trys) stop while the word is still sounding: the July recorder stopped early and the old files hid it with added silence. They are on the batch 2 page, section 'July'. My recommendation: put the A1 ones back on your sheet as re-takes (a few minutes of recording); their current takes stay in the deck until the new ones arrive, so nothing goes silent. title: Loudness: add a gentle limiter to the new takes?
ask: Your July takes were peak-limited (median −16.7 LUFS); the new ones use plain gain only and sit about 2 dB quieter (median −18.8 to −19.2). Matching July needs a gentle limiter, 2–5 dB on peaks only. Plain gain is the safer, cleaner processing; 2 dB is a small step most listeners won't notice between cards. Unanswered = no limiter.

title: Stress the forms the dictionaries couldn't (97 in A1)
ask: 949 genitives, feminines and verb forms now carry stress marks sourced from Wiktionary. 353 couldn't be sourced: missing from the dictionary, an unstressed table, or two variants the headword doesn't decide (e.g. raudóna / raudonà). The sheet is rounds/2026-10-28_stress_forms/OWNER_SHEET_v1.csv in the 51.04 folder (also attached in the chat), A1 first in study order. Also fixed from the source: antis 'duck' is feminine, gen ánties (the card had añtis 'bosom''s ančio); kaltas 'guilty' is kal̃tas, kaltà. title: AnkiWeb description and the choices in it
ask: The text is below, with the counts of rc4; every number (cards, audio) is recounted from rc5 before upload, so the audio paragraph will say nearly all of A1 is in your voice. Decide: (1) sign it with your name, or keep "the author"; (2) the share title; (3) the tags; (4) replace the old v2.0 share, or keep both; (5) licence CC BY-NC 4.0, as in the repo's LICENSE. Write your choices in the note.
options: Approve with the changes in my note
detail:
### The text

**Lietuvių Flashcards — A1 (v3.0)**

Lithuanian from zero to A1 through pictures, phrases and sentences. The first of two subdecks; A2 follows as a separate package.

**What is in the deck**

1,191 cards, ordered by usefulness: survival words and everyday phrases come first.

- 687 picture cards for words
- 135 phrase cards (greetings, thanks, asking for things)
- 334 cloze cards for function words and forms
- 35 sentence cards with a picture

**How a card works**

The front shows a picture with an English caption in the band below it. The back gives the Lithuanian word with its stress mark, gender and forms (genitive, present and past, or the feminine), and the English gloss. Phrase cards add a note on when to use the phrase. Cloze cards show a Lithuanian sentence with a blank and the English as a hint; sentence cards pair the blank with a picture.

Stress marks are taken from Wiktionary, kirtis.info and the LKŽ, never guessed.

**The pictures**

The art is an original house style: a civil-defence training manual from a free Lithuania of 1981. The pictures are AI-generated in that style and reviewed by hand. A few cards show real interwar places and people: the Lituanica with Darius and Girėnas, Basanavičius as the doctor, Čiurlionis as the artist, with a painting after one of his public-domain works on the easel.

**Audio**

547 cards carry recordings by the author, a native speaker, reading the word and its forms. 20 older cards still use a synthetic voice, and the other 624 are silent until the next update.

Fonts: Brygada 1918 (SIL Open Font Licence), embedded. In night mode, leave image inversion off.

**Upgrading from an earlier version**

The note types changed in v3.0. Delete the old deck before importing this one; study history from older versions does not carry over. The card IDs will be locked once the A2 subdeck is out; from then on, updates import in place and keep your progress. Until then, an update may ask you to delete and re-import.

**Licence and credits**

CC BY-NC 4.0: share and adapt for non-commercial use, with credit and a link to the source. Word list from the Fluent Forever 625, extended from A1 English word lists. Pictures, data and recordings by the author.

Source and issues: https://github.com/dainius-sileika/Lithuanian_Flashcards

### The choices, with background

1. **Licence wording.** The repo `LICENSE` is CC BY-NC 4.0 (not BY-NC-SA) and names the owner in the required attribution string. The text follows it. If a different licence is wanted for the published deck, change `LICENSE` first, then this line.
2. **Signing the description.** The rule "name no living person" was applied to the owner too: the text says "the author" and leaves the credit to the GitHub link and `LICENSE`. Decide whether to sign it with a name.
3. **Audio sentence.** The brief said "the 520 core cards have native-speaker recordings"; the data says otherwise. `audio_source.tsv` marks 427 recordings as human and 93 as `azure-neural` (the files differ: 48 kbps, no ID3 tag). On 2026-10-19, of the 446 base cards in the A1 block, 427 were human, 18 synthetic, 1 without audio (`0007_batonas`); the 75 base rows with `level = A2` are exactly the 75 remaining synthetic ones. If the 18 were re-recorded without updating the ledger, correct the ledger first. The retag for order v3 may move some of these between subdecks; recount from the manifest.
4. **Historical cards left out on purpose.** Gustaitis (2263_inzinierius), the 1939 basketball team (138 komanda, `level = A2`; 1405_krepsinis) and the two posters (*Velnio nuotaka* on 1473_siaip_sau, *Milžino paunksmė* on 1419_spektaklis) are A2-level rows and not in this package. They belong in the A2 description. 097 prezidentas and 123 autorius ship without likenesses. If order v3 retags any of them A1, add them to "The pictures".
5. **Title** for the AnkiWeb share, e.g. "Lietuvių Flashcards — Lithuanian A1 (pictures, audio, stress marks)". Decide also whether the v2.0 share is replaced or kept (F3).
6. **Tags** on AnkiWeb, e.g. `lithuanian lietuvių a1 vocabulary pictures audio`.

title: Proofreading: your 25 corrections, how they went in
ask: 11 went in as you wrote them. 2 cards switch to your word, because it wasn't a card yet: veikla → užsiėmimas (Mėgstu užsiėmimus lauke.) and draustis → apsidrausti (Prieš kelionę reikia apsidrausti.). For 13, your sentence dropped the word the card teaches. Mostly your word already has its own card (Kiek jums metų?, Peršalau, šiek tiek, du kartus, reikia, užrakinti…); in the rest the old word is worth keeping as a card. So these cards keep their word in a new everyday sentence. Your sentence is saved as the reason. Kuri valanda? becomes Kelinta valanda?, and the kelinta card gets Kelinta šiandien? instead. Below are the 13 new sentences: if one sounds off, write your version in the note, otherwise nothing to do. One side effect: the usage note on the back of Kelinta valanda? was withdrawn, because it explained Kuri valanda?.
